attributes.residual:
UNCHANGED at real 24, insns T450/O450, opcode multiset IDENTICAL. This TU (game/world/btricol) is 6-of-7 exact and BTriLineCol is the only function blocking the flip.

THE DEF-COUNT CENSUS THE WORK ORDER ASKED FOR, RUN AND REPORTED. Every FP-defining opcode in both streams was classified by destination FPR (script: fnasm dump of target and ours, destination of lfs/lfd/fmr/fadds/fsubs/fmuls/fdivs/fsel/frsp/fctiwz/... families). Only FOUR registers differ in def count across 450 instructions: f0 target 70 / ours 69; f3 target 8 / ours 9; f23 target 2 / ours 1; f24 target 1 / ours 2. Live spans: target f2 begins 0xe8, ours f2 begins 0xfc; target f3 begins 0x15c, ours f3 begins 0xe8; target f23 spans 0x3c-0x200 with 2 defs, ours 0x174-0x200 with 1; target f24 spans 0x170-0x1fc with 1 def, ours 0x3c-0x1fc with 2. So the residual is exactly TWO register-identity swaps, not a diffuse colouring: (A) the volatile temp loaded at 0xe8 from 204(r1) is target f2 / ours f3, which cascades to the 0.0 remat at 0xfc landing in target f0 / ours f2; (B) a clean two-way swap of the callee-saved pair f23/f24, distinguished only by which web is allocated first (target gives f23 to the web that opens at 0x3c, we give it f24).

WHAT THE CENSUS SETTLES. The work order's hypothesis was that the discriminant is home-register interference and that SHORTENING our fresh register's web would flip the choice. The census says the interference reading is DIRECTIONALLY CORRECT but is a consequence, not a lever: the target rematerializes 0.0 into f0, its MAXIMALLY reused scratch (70 defs, the single busiest register in the function), precisely because in the target's colouring f2 is already occupied by the 0xe8 temp; our colouring leaves f2 free at 0xfc, so our allocator spends it on the constant. Both sides pick the lowest-numbered register that is free under their own colouring - the rule is identical and the INPUT differs. There is no web to shorten: our 0xfc value is already dead by 0x110 on the fallthrough path; what keeps it observable is not its length but which def the LATER use binds to.

THE REAL MECHANISM, NOW NAMED PRECISELY (this supersedes v3's 'rematerialization REGISTER choice'). Source lines 243-245 are `if ((tpB.y > K && tpA.y > K) || (tpB.y < *(volatile const f64*)&K && tpA.y < K))` with K = lbl_80345D40 = 0.0. Both streams emit exactly TWO loads of K: one at 0xfc serving the first clause, one at 0x114 forced by the volatile cast. The divergence is a single def-USE BINDING: the plain read on line 245 binds, in the target, to the LATER load at 0x114 (`fcmpo cr0,f2,f0`), and in ours to the EARLIER load at 0xfc (`fcmpo cr0,f3,f2`), leaving our first value alive across the reload. Numerically identical, structurally one binding apart, and it is why webfrank_audit rejects at +0x120 rather than anywhere else.

NEW AXIS MEASURED AND REFUTED, WITH A REUSABLE LAW. If our compiler could be made to update its CSE entry at the volatile load, line 245 would bind to it and the whole cascade would align. Probe: put a volatile cast on the FIRST clause too (`tpB.y > *(volatile const f64*)&K && tpA.y > K`), untried and distinct from v3's axis 7 (which REMOVED the existing volatile). Result REGRESSED real 24 -> 126, insns T450/O452, `ours-only: -2 lfd`, inserted loads at 0x10c and 0x124. The failure is unambiguous and general: each volatile read emitted its OWN load AND the neighbouring plain reads still emitted theirs, i.e. a plain read NEVER binds to a volatile load's result in this compiler. Banked as claim.law.bb-plain-read-never-cse-binds-to-a-volatile-load.20260901.v1. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS FUNCTION, and it is the important one: since a plain read cannot bind to a volatile load HERE, the target's 0x120 binding to the 0x114 load PROVES the target's 0x114 load is NOT volatile-driven - retail simply rematerialized the pool constant twice and bound each use to its nearest def. Our `*(volatile const f64*)` cast is reconstruction SCAFFOLD that buys the correct instruction COUNT while making the correct BINDING unreachable by construction. The residual is therefore structural to the scaffold, and the honest closure is for our build to rematerialize the constant where it currently CSEs it - a compiler-internal decision with no source spelling in reach.

DO NOT RETRY: v3's axes 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 (each a measured regression or a matched pair of identical results) and this pass's volatile-on-first-clause axis. The remaining live ideas are (i) an image-wide census of the plain-vs-volatile pool-constant scaffold to size the class before anyone spends more probes on it, and (ii) the value-equivalence guard extension across equal-valued defs that v2 already specified - still the only named honest closure, and it must be a SOUND guard extension, never an audit escape.
